body.name: stripe.com
body.ctaMessage: Strong foundation. Real gaps in the experience layer.
body.agenticSummary: Stripe offers solid developer resource discoverability, but lacks a published OpenAPI specification.

checks.name: ARD discovery
checks.details: No /.well-known/ard.json (and no legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json)
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agentic Resource Discovery catalog at /.well-known/ard.json so AI clients can discover your agentic resources (MCP servers, agents, skills, APIs). See https://agenticresourcediscovery.org/

checks.name: AI Catalog discovery
checks.details: No /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - the AI Catalog Standard's discovery path. Bonus only; a catalog at /.well-known/ard.json is scored by the ARD discovery check.
checks.recommendation: Serve a valid catalog at /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - the AI Catalog Standard's own discovery path - so consumers following that spec (see https://ai-catalog.io/) also find you. The same document you serve at /.well-known/ard.json works unchanged.

checks.name: ARD entry validity
checks.details: No catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - entry validity applies only to published catalogs
checks.recommendation: Make every catalog entry fully valid: a domain-anchored urn:air identifier, a displayName, a media type, and exactly one of url or data. Applies to the catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or the legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json.

checks.name: ARD trust manifest
checks.details: No catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - trust metadata applies only to published catalogs
checks.recommendation: Add a trustManifest (verifiable identity, compliance attestations, or signature) to your catalog entries (ard.json, or the legacy ai-catalog.json) so clients can verify your resources with progressive trust.

checks.name: Category share of voice
checks.details: Category share of voice is in beta. It measures whether agents surface you for capability and use-case searches (not just your name). We are tuning it for accuracy before it counts toward your score - coming soon as a Pro check.
checks.recommendation: Build topical authority for your category. Publish comparison pages, 'best X for Y' content, tutorials, and integration guides that rank for generic use-case queries - not just your brand name - so agents surface you when users describe a need.

checks.name: Developer resource discoverability
checks.details: Agent discovered 2 developer-resource types by name (MCP server, API docs) across 3 pages
checks.recommendation: Check whether your developer resources (API docs, OpenAPI spec, auth docs, developer portal, MCP server, SDK documentation) surface in name-based searches. If they do not, use predictable URLs, link them in llms.txt, and include your product name in page titles and headings. This result reflects one search sample.

checks.name: Brand name discoverability
checks.details: stripe.com appears 5 times in brand-name search results for "Stripe payments fintech" (top position: #4)
checks.recommendation: Make sure a clean search for your brand name returns your own domain in the top results. If it does not, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen brand-name search by claiming consistent NAP across listings, earning press mentions that link to the canonical domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask the apex domain in search results.

checks.name: Wikipedia / Wikidata entity presence
checks.details: Wikipedia "Stripe, Inc." and Wikidata Q7624104 both verified - domain confirmed on both sources
checks.recommendation: Establish a Wikipedia article and a Wikidata entity for your brand, with the domain set as the official website (Wikidata property P856) and a corresponding external link on Wikipedia. Wikipedia is the largest single source of citations in ChatGPT and a primary input to Knowledge Graphs across Google, Bing, and LLM training data. Earn third-party press coverage first to satisfy notability, then draft the article with cited references rather than self-promotion.

checks.name: robots.txt AI crawler policy
checks.details: Training: 12/12. Search: 18/18 page/crawler pairs permitted. No applicable crawl or usage restriction found for 5 training and search crawlers (gptbot, claudebot, oai-searchbot, claude-searchbot, perplexitybot) on 6 public pages: https://stripe.com/, https://stripe.com/legal/end-customer-ach-payments-authorization, https://stripe.com/legal/bank-of-ayudhya-acquirer-terms, https://stripe.com/legal/ftb-issuing-offer-document, https://stripe.com/legal/consumer/pay-by-bank-payment-initiation-services, https://stripe.com/legal/stripe-event-speaker-release. Declared policy only; absence of a Content Signal expresses no usage preference. Paths outside this sample, live bot access, indexing, and model training are not verified
checks.recommendation: For broad training and search readiness, permit GPTBot and ClaudeBot to collect the affected public pages for training, and OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, and PerplexityBot to crawl them for search. Review the reported URLs, rule lines, and applicable ai-train or search Content Signals. Keep private and account paths restricted. General permissions already count; named directives and Content Signals are optional. The paired search=yes, ai-train=no retains full credit when all evaluated crawling and search are permitted. Other training restrictions mean partial coverage under this benchmark. Usage permission never overrides Disallow. Use the existing agent-user policy and live access results to assess visits.

checks.name: Listed in MCP registries
checks.details: Verified in 2 registries: Smithery (stripe) [verified-curation], npm (@stripe/mcp) [npm-scope] - 48 agent uses, verified
checks.recommendation: Register your MCP server on Smithery (smithery.ai) or mcp.so so agent platforms can discover your tools. Link the registry entry from your homepage or docs for bi-directional verification.

checks.name: NPM/PyPI SDK package
checks.details: NPM package found: stripe - "Stripe API wrapper"
checks.recommendation: Publish a JavaScript/TypeScript SDK package on npm so developers can integrate your API programmatically. In package.json set `repository` to your source repo and `homepage` to your product domain - these links are how agents confirm the package is your official SDK rather than a third-party tool with a similar name.

checks.name: Agent platform configs
checks.details: Could not locate a public repo containing agent configs or rules. If our probes missed it, AI coding agents likely will too - link the repo from your homepage or docs so it's discoverable.
checks.recommendation: Add an AGENTS.md or .cursorrules file to your public GitHub repo with instructions for how AI coding agents should interact with your codebase. Then make sure the repo is documented in the entry-point pages agents read - homepage, docs, and llms.txt - so it can be discovered without guessing.

checks.name: Agent Plugins manifest
checks.details: No Agent Plugins manifest (plugin.json) found in discovered repos
checks.recommendation: Bundle your agent skills and MCP servers as an Agent Plugin: add a plugin.json manifest with the agent-plugins.org $schema and a name. See https://agent-plugins.org/specification

checks.name: Listed on skills.sh
checks.details: No official skills self-published on skills.sh
checks.recommendation: Publish agent skills on skills.sh so AI agents can discover your product's capabilities. Create a SKILL.md in your GitHub repo and register it with 'npx skills add'. See skills.sh/docs.

checks.name: Registry branding
checks.details: No registry branding (name, icon, description) found
checks.recommendation: Give your MCP server-card (at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json) a display name, an icon or logo, and a description - all three together are what reads as a complete, branded listing agents can present.

checks.name: ChatGPT app listed
checks.details: Found in ChatGPT app directory: "Stripe"
checks.recommendation: Submit your app to the ChatGPT apps / connectors directory (the apps-in-ChatGPT surface) so ChatGPT users can discover and use your product.

checks.name: Sitemap exists
checks.details: Valid sitemap found at https://stripe.com/sitemap/sitemap.xml with multiple sitemaps entries
checks.recommendation: Add a valid XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml listing all indexable URLs. Include lastmod dates and keep it under 50MB.

checks.name: Content without JavaScript
checks.details: 10440 chars with H1, but 2.7% content ratio is below the 5% target
checks.recommendation: Serve at least 500 characters of meaningful homepage content in raw HTML. Add a clear H1, keep deeper heading levels sequential, and remove excessive non-content markup.

checks.name: Not blocked by bot detection
checks.details: Site accessible to 6 AI agent user-agents
checks.recommendation: Allowlist known AI agent User-Agents (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, DeepSeekBot) in your WAF or bot-detection rules.

checks.name: Agent discovery file
checks.details: No agent discovery file found
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent Skills index at /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json that lists your capabilities, with each skill carrying a name and a description so agents can find and parse what you offer.

checks.name: Agent Skills index conformance (v0.2.0)
checks.details: No /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json - skip v0.2.0 conformance
checks.recommendation: Upgrade /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json to the v0.2.0 schema: add "$schema": "https://schemas.agentskills.io/discovery/0.2.0/schema.json", and give every entry a type (skill-md or archive), url, and digest. Use "digest": "sha256:<64 lowercase hex chars>" (e.g. "digest": "sha256:a3f1...") - a bare "sha256": "<hex>" field is also accepted. Compute the value from the artifact's raw bytes.

checks.name: A2A / agent-card
checks.details: No A2A agent card found at /.well-known/agent-card.json
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json describing your agent's capabilities, skills, and contact endpoint.

checks.name: pricing.md exists
checks.details: No pricing.md found - agents need machine-readable pricing to compare products and make purchase recommendations
checks.recommendation: Create a /pricing.md file with your pricing tiers, features, and limits in plain markdown. This lets AI agents compare costs and recommend plans without scraping HTML pricing pages.

checks.name: NLWeb Schema Feeds
checks.details: No schemamap: directive in robots.txt
checks.recommendation: Add a schemamap: directive to robots.txt pointing to a Schema Map XML file listing your structured data feeds (JSONL/RSS). See the NLWeb Schema Feeds spec.

checks.name: MCP well-known discovery
checks.details: MCP server at https://mcp.stripe.com - consider adding /.well-known/mcp for standard discovery
checks.recommendation: Serve your MCP server at /.well-known/mcp, publish a server-card.json at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, or reference it in llms.txt so agents can discover it automatically without manual URL input.

checks.name: Agent mode view
checks.details: Rich agent mode view at ?mode=agent with 6 agent signals and navigation links
checks.recommendation: Add a ?mode=agent query parameter to your homepage that returns a structured, machine-readable view with API endpoints, authentication info, and key capabilities instead of marketing HTML.

checks.name: HTTP Link headers (RFC 8288)
checks.details: No HTTP Link response headers (RFC 8288) found
checks.recommendation: Add HTTP Link: response headers (RFC 8288) advertising your sitemap, markdown alternates, API service descriptions, and API catalog. Example: Link: </sitemap.xml>; rel="sitemap", </index.md>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown".

checks.name: Markdown URL fallback
checks.details: Homepage does not support the .md suffix. Probed https://stripe.com/index.md and it did not return markdown (expected text/markdown content-type or a heading-led non-HTML body). Serve /index.md so agents can fetch one canonical markdown URL for the site root.
checks.recommendation: Let agents fetch markdown by appending .md to page URLs. Required for any credit: serve a markdown homepage at /index.md. For full credit (2/2): also serve a .md twin for each content page (e.g. /docs/auth -> /docs/auth.md). Content-Type should be text/markdown and the body should start with a top-level heading (not HTML).

checks.name: Modular llms.txt per product area
checks.details: Only 1 section-level llms.txt found (docs) - add at least one more (/docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt) to earn bonus credit
checks.recommendation: Add per-section llms.txt files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt, /developers/llms.txt) so agents can fetch scoped context for specific product areas instead of the whole manual.

checks.name: Sitemap freshness (lastmod)
checks.details: None of the 500 sampled sitemap entries carries a lastmod date. Add <lastmod> (W3C datetime) so agents can prioritize fresh content.
checks.recommendation: Add <lastmod> dates (W3C datetime, e.g. 2026-08-01) to your sitemap entries and update them when content actually changes. Aim for lastmod on at least half your entries with the newest within the last year. Verify with `curl https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml | grep lastmod`.

checks.name: robots.txt agent-user policy
checks.details: No applicable crawl or usage restriction found for 3 user-triggered agents (chatgpt-user, claude-user, perplexity-user) on 1 public page: https://stripe.com/. Declared policy only; absence of a Content Signal expresses no usage preference. Paths outside this sample, live bot access, indexing, and model training are not verified
checks.recommendation: Review the matched homepage rules for ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, and Perplexity-User. If you intend to permit these requests, remove or narrow the reported restriction while keeping private paths protected. Review applicable ai-input=no declarations if answer-time use is intended. This check reports declared permission; a robots.txt change alone does not establish live access.

checks.name: llms.txt exists
checks.details: Found the llms.txt at https://stripe.com/llms.txt.
checks.recommendation: Create an llms.txt file at your domain root (/llms.txt) - the AI equivalent of robots.txt. Write at least 100 characters of real content: what your product is, what it does, and links to your key docs. Then verify it with `curl https://yourdomain.com/llms.txt` - you should see your text, not HTML. If your app returns its homepage for every URL (common with single-page apps), add a static file route so the raw text is served. A placeholder with just a heading earns no credit.

checks.name: llms.txt formatting
checks.details: The llms.txt is well-formatted with markdown links, but at 92,252 characters it exceeds the 30,000-character recommendation for a navigation index.
checks.recommendation: Format your llms.txt as a navigation index: start with a markdown heading, include markdown links to deeper resources, and keep it under 30,000 characters. If you have more to say, move long-form content into /llms-full.txt or per-section files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt) and link to them from the main index.

checks.name: JSON-LD structured data
checks.details: Rich JSON-LD identity: Organization with name, description, url, and sameAs/logo/address (1 block(s))
checks.recommendation: Add JSON-LD structured data to your homepage using the identity type that matches your site - SoftwareApplication for products, Organization or LocalBusiness for companies, Person for personal sites, Article for blogs - with name, description, url, and type-appropriate fields (offers, sameAs, author) so AI can parse your identity programmatically.

checks.name: Pricing info accessible
checks.details: Pricing page found at /pricing
checks.recommendation: Make pricing discoverable - add a /pricing page or include pricing as schema.org/Offer structured data, so agents can find it without scraping a marketing page.

checks.name: Public API/docs linked from homepage
checks.details: Documentation site found at https://docs.stripe.com
checks.recommendation: Publish API documentation at a discoverable URL (/docs, /api, /developers). Include authentication, endpoints, and example requests.

checks.name: Agent instruction / when-to-use
checks.details: When-to-use guidance found in llms.txt
checks.recommendation: Tell agents when to reach for you: add a 'when to use this' section to your llms.txt (or a dedicated agent-instructions file) that names your best-fit use cases and how an agent should call you. Be specific about the jobs you are right for - generic marketing copy does not read as guidance.

checks.name: Skills.sh skill quality
checks.details: No official skills on skills.sh to evaluate
checks.recommendation: Expand your skills.sh presence with multiple skill repos covering different use cases. Add descriptive skill names, clear SKILL.md files, and organize by capability area.

checks.name: JSON-LD entity linking (sameAs)
checks.details: Strong entity linking via sameAs: linkedin.com, wikipedia.org, crunchbase.com, github.com, wikidata.org
checks.recommendation: Add sameAs links in your JSON-LD structured data pointing to your Wikipedia page, Wikidata entry, GitHub org, and social profiles. This helps AI disambiguate your brand from similarly named entities.

checks.name: Metadata completeness
checks.details: All metadata signals present: canonical URL, lang="en-US", og:image, og:type
checks.recommendation: Add all four signals to your homepage: <link rel="canonical">, <html lang="...">, <meta property="og:image">, and <meta property="og:type">. Agents use these for entity resolution and attribution.

checks.name: Organization schema completeness
checks.details: Organization schema found but missing: address
checks.recommendation: Add Organization JSON-LD that includes both contactPoint (with email/phone and contactType) and address (PostalAddress). This lets AI verify your business legitimacy and answer contact queries.

checks.name: Schema type breadth
checks.details: No extended schema types found - AI can only answer basic questions about this entity
checks.recommendation: Expand your JSON-LD beyond Organization/WebSite. Add FAQPage for common questions, Service or Product for offerings, AggregateRating or Review for social proof, and BreadcrumbList for navigation context.

checks.name: Trust anchor pages
checks.details: All trust anchor pages verified: About, Contact, Privacy
checks.recommendation: Publish real /about, /contact, and /privacy pages with at least 500 characters of content each. These are the pages AI agents check to verify your business is legitimate before recommending you.

checks.name: llms.txt links resolve
checks.details: All 5 probed llms.txt links resolve to real content
checks.recommendation: Make every link your llms.txt declares resolve to real content. Verify each one with `curl -L <url>` - you should see the linked document, not your homepage. If your app returns the homepage shell for unknown paths (common with single-page apps), a 200 status is not proof: check the body. Fix or remove any dead link; agents that follow the index treat a broken link as a dead end.

checks.name: Markdown alternate link
checks.details: No sampled page advertises a markdown alternate. Add <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="..."> (or the equivalent Link response header) pointing at a markdown twin of the page.
checks.recommendation: Advertise a markdown twin of each page with <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="..."> in the HTML head (or an equivalent Link response header), and make sure the advertised URL actually serves markdown - an advertisement pointing at HTML is worse than none. Verify the target with `curl -s <href>` and check the body starts with a heading, not <!doctype html>.

checks.name: Markdown frontmatter metadata
checks.details: No served markdown found (no root .md docs, no Accept: text/markdown negotiation) - nothing to carry frontmatter
checks.recommendation: Open your served markdown docs with a --- frontmatter block carrying title plus at least one of description, canonical, or last-updated. Agents read frontmatter as document metadata without scraping. A Link: rel="canonical" response header also satisfies the canonical slot.

checks.name: Redirect hygiene
checks.details: No meta-refresh stubs, JavaScript-redirect stubs, or cross-domain hops across 6 checked pages
checks.recommendation: Replace meta-refresh and JavaScript-only redirects with real HTTP 301/302 redirects. Non-JS agents never execute `location.href` or wait for a meta refresh - they see only the stub page. Verify with `curl -sI <url>` - you should see a Location header, not a 200 with a near-empty body.

checks.name: Page token budget
checks.details: All 6 measured pages fit an agent context budget (largest ~5K tokens)
checks.recommendation: Keep each page's extracted text under ~100K characters (~25K tokens) so it fits an agent's context window without truncation. Split oversized reference pages into focused per-topic documents and link them from an index. Check a page with `curl -s <url> | wc -c` and remember agents read the extracted text, not the raw HTML.

checks.name: Code fence validity
checks.details: Code fences balanced across 1 markdown document
checks.recommendation: Close every fenced code block (``` or ~~~) in your served markdown. CommonMark treats everything after an unclosed fence as code, so an agent parsing the document silently loses the rest of it. Count fence lines per file - the total must be even.

checks.name: Content behind auth
checks.details: All 5 sampled pages are publicly readable (5 with substantive content)
checks.recommendation: Serve your content pages without a login wall. Agents cannot complete auth flows while browsing - a 401/403 or a login-form page is invisible content. Keep public documentation public; if some content must stay gated, publish an ungated summary so agents can still represent it.

checks.name: OpenAPI spec published
checks.details: No OpenAPI/Swagger specification found
checks.recommendation: Publish an OpenAPI (Swagger) specification at /openapi.json or /api/openapi.yaml. This is how agents understand your API surface automatically.

checks.name: Developer portal
checks.details: Developer portal found at /docs
checks.recommendation: Create a developer portal at /developers with API keys, documentation, quickstart guides, and a sandbox environment.

checks.name: API catalog (RFC 9727)
checks.details: No /.well-known/api-catalog found (RFC 9727)
checks.recommendation: Publish an API catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog per RFC 9727. Serve it with Content-Type: application/linkset+json;profile="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9727" and include a 'linkset' array with item entries pointing to your OpenAPI specs and service descriptions.

checks.name: Markdown agent docs
checks.details: Missing markdown content negotiation. Homepage returned text/html when probed with Accept: text/markdown (expected text/markdown), and none of the well-known root paths (/llms.md, /auth.md, /agents.md, /developers.md, /api.md, /index.md, /skill.md, /agent.md, /developer.md) returned markdown. Cold-arrival agents that land on the homepage from web search cannot get a markdown representation - serve text/markdown on the homepage via Accept negotiation, or publish a static /llms.md at the root.
checks.recommendation: Pick one: (a) return Content-Type: text/markdown on GET <homepage> when the request sends Accept: text/markdown, or (b) publish a static /llms.md, /auth.md, or /agents.md file at your root with real markdown content. Option (b) is usually a single static file. This is the cold-discovery path for agents that land at your homepage from web search without reading llms.txt first.

checks.name: Markdown content negotiation (acceptmarkdown.com)
checks.details: Homepage https://stripe.com does not meet the Markdown negotiation requirements: Accept: text/markdown returned text/html; charset=utf-8; Vary header missing Accept (got "none")
checks.recommendation: Enable Markdown negotiation on the scanned homepage. Supporting it only on /docs or a separate .md URL does not satisfy this check. Requests with Accept: text/markdown must receive a nonempty Markdown body with Content-Type: text/markdown and Vary: Accept. Keep serving HTML for Accept: text/html. Adding Vary alone does not create a Markdown response. Verify both with `curl -sS -L -i -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://yourdomain.com/` and `curl -sS -L -i -H 'Accept: text/html' https://yourdomain.com/`. Check the final response headers and body: Markdown with Vary: Accept for the first request, HTML for the second.

checks.name: Bot-UA markdown serving
checks.details: https://docs.stripe.com serves markdown to the GPTBot User-Agent even with Accept: text/html - UA-sniffed agent responses in place
checks.recommendation: Optionally detect AI-bot User-Agents (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) server-side and serve them a markdown representation of the page directly, even when they send Accept: text/html. Verify with `curl -A "ClaudeBot/1.0" https://yourdomain.com/` - a markdown body earns this bonus. Accept-header negotiation is scored separately.

checks.name: Agent crawler reachability
checks.details: Reachable to all major AI crawlers - ChatGPT-User: reachable, ClaudeBot: reachable, Google-Extended: reachable, ora-agent: reachable, DeepSeekBot: reachable
checks.recommendation: Allowlist the major AI crawler/agent User-Agents (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, ora-agent, DeepSeekBot) in your WAF, bot-detection rules, and robots.txt so agents can reach your homepage.

checks.name: MCP tool descriptions
checks.details: product MCP requires authentication - cannot enumerate tools to evaluate descriptions (N/A)

checks.name: MCP parameter schemas
checks.details: product MCP requires authentication - cannot enumerate tools to evaluate parameter schemas (N/A)

checks.name: MCP server identity
checks.details: product MCP requires authentication - cannot read server identity from handshake (N/A)

checks.name: MCP tool listing
checks.details: product MCP requires authentication - cannot list tools (N/A)

checks.name: MCP tool naming
checks.details: product MCP requires authentication - cannot enumerate tools to evaluate naming (N/A)

checks.name: Public API with reachable endpoints
checks.details: REST API documentation found at https://docs.stripe.com/sandboxes.md. Best-of-protocols score: 7/7.
checks.recommendation: Expose a public REST or GraphQL API. AI agents need programmatic access  - not just a web UI  - to integrate with your product.

checks.name: OAuth 2.0 support
checks.details: OAuth authorization server metadata at https://access.stripe.com/mcp
checks.recommendation: Implement OAuth 2.0 for API authentication. Publish your authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

checks.name: Scoped permissions
checks.details: Scoped permissions described at https://docs.stripe.com, but no machine-readable scope declaration found (OpenAPI oauth2 scopes or RFC 9728 scopes_supported)
checks.recommendation: Declare scoped API permissions where machines can read them: named OAuth scopes in your OpenAPI security schemes, or scopes_supported in RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata. Prose descriptions of roles help humans, but agents need the machine-readable declaration to request least-privilege access.

checks.name: MCP auth mechanism
checks.details: product MCP requires authentication with OAuth metadata discovery
checks.recommendation: Protect your MCP server with OAuth 2.0 authentication. Publish authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server for automatic agent auth flows.

checks.name: MCP OAuth metadata
checks.details: RFC 8414 OAuth metadata for product MCP: issuer=https://access.stripe.com/mcp, auth and token endpoints present; client registration: DCR endpoint only (RFC 7591, deprecated in favor of CIMD)
checks.recommendation: Publish RFC 8414 authorization server metadata with issuer, authorization_endpoint, and token_endpoint so agents can authenticate without hardcoded URLs. For client registration, advertise client_id_metadata_document_supported (CIMD) - Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated and worth keeping only as a compatibility path.

checks.name: MCP PKCE S256 support
checks.details: OAuth metadata for product MCP supports PKCE S256 code challenge
checks.recommendation: Support PKCE with S256 code challenge method in your OAuth server. Add 'S256' to code_challenge_methods_supported in your authorization server metadata.

checks.name: Agent onboarding friction
checks.details: Onboarding signals described but not verified live: free tier available, self-serve key generation, sandbox/test environment
checks.recommendation: Offer a free tier or trial, self-serve API key generation, and a sandbox environment. Agents can't fill out 'contact sales' forms.

checks.name: Web Bot Auth directory
checks.details: No /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory found
checks.recommendation: Publish a Web Bot Auth directory at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory. Serve a JSON document with a 'keys' array of Ed25519 JWKs (kty=OKP, crv=Ed25519, kid, nbf, exp). This lets agents sign their requests per RFC 9421 so you can distinguish legitimate bots from spoofers.

checks.name: OAuth Protected Resource metadata (RFC 9728)
checks.details: RFC 9728 metadata at https://mcp.stripe.com: resource=https://mcp.stripe.com, authorization_servers (1)
checks.recommendation: Publish RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. Include the resource field plus enough supporting metadata - your authorization servers, supported scopes, accepted bearer methods - that an agent can work out how to authenticate without first triggering a 401.

checks.name: auth.md exists
checks.details: No /auth.md found at site root
checks.recommendation: Publish /auth.md as a markdown prose walkthrough of how agents should obtain credentials. Serve it with Content-Type: text/markdown, lead with a top-level heading, and write at least ~200 chars of real content (not just a placeholder). See the WorkOS auth.md spec at https://github.com/workos/auth.md.

checks.name: auth.md structure
checks.details: No /auth.md found at site root
checks.recommendation: Structure /auth.md as the WorkOS spec prescribes: sections for Discover, Pick a method, Register, Claim, Exchange, Use the access_token, Errors, and Revocation, with spec anchor keywords (agent_auth, identity_endpoint, identity_assertion, service_auth, id-jag, WWW-Authenticate). Reference https://github.com/workos/auth.md.

checks.name: auth.md walkthrough simulation
checks.details: /auth.md not found at site root
checks.recommendation: Make your published auth-discovery chain traversable end to end: an agent starting at /auth.md (or your protected-resource metadata) should be able to follow the links to your authorization-server metadata and registration endpoint without hitting a dead link. Test the whole path, not just each file in isolation.

checks.name: Agent auth discovery metadata

checks.recommendation: If agents transact on your site, expose an MPP 402 challenge (WWW-Authenticate: Payment) or advertise x-payment-info in your OpenAPI spec.

checks.name: x402 payment protocol
checks.details: No x402 payment protocol support detected
checks.recommendation: If agents transact on your site, return a 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (x402 schema) or publish an x402 Bazaar discovery endpoint at /discovery/resources.

checks.name: UCP - Universal Commerce Protocol
checks.details: text mentions (universal commerce protocol, checkout-sessions) but no /.well-known/ucp profile or commerce metadata
checks.recommendation: Publish a UCP discovery profile at /.well-known/ucp with a valid `version` (YYYY-MM-DD).

checks.name: ACP - Agentic Commerce Protocol
checks.details: ACP text signals (agentic commerce protocol, shared payment token, shared-payment-token) plus ACP request headers (API-Version / Idempotency-Key); no live /checkout_sessions endpoint on https://stripe.com or https://api.stripe.com; OPTIONS allows POST at https://api.stripe.com/checkout_sessions but POST 404 returned no ACP-shaped response
checks.recommendation: Implement the Agentic Commerce Protocol checkout REST API: `POST /checkout_sessions` (create), update/get/complete/cancel variants, with `API-Version: YYYY-MM-DD` and `Idempotency-Key` required headers. Preflight OPTIONS should allow POST or return an ACP-shaped error with `supported_versions` so agents can negotiate.

checks.name: ACP delegate payment
checks.details: Delegate Payment text signals (shared payment token); no reachable /agentic_commerce/delegate_payment endpoint on https://stripe.com or https://api.stripe.com; OPTIONS allows POST at https://api.stripe.com/agentic_commerce/delegate_payment but POST 404 returned no ACP-shaped response
checks.recommendation: Expose the ACP Delegate Payment endpoint at `POST /agentic_commerce/delegate_payment`. The request takes `payment_method`, `allowance` (max amount, currency, expiry, merchant scope), and `risk_signals`; the response returns a vault token. This lets agents pay on behalf of users with scoped, revocable credentials.

checks.name: AP2 - Agent Payments Protocol
checks.details: No AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) signals detected
checks.recommendation: Adopt Google's AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol): advertise an AP2 mandate capability in your UCP discovery profile and verify the Intent / Cart / Payment mandates (SD-JWT verifiable digital credentials) server-side before settling.

topFixes.name: OpenAPI spec published
topFixes.recommendation: Publish an OpenAPI (Swagger) specification at /openapi.json or /api/openapi.yaml. This is how agents understand your API surface automatically.

topFixes.name: WebMCP support
topFixes.recommendation: Expose in-page tools through WebMCP, a proposed web standard for browser agents. Register tools with document.modelContext.registerTool() and use navigator.modelContext only as a trailing compatibility fallback. Declarative forms with toolname and tooldescription provide server-rendered evidence, but remain a preview and should not be your only tool surface. Chrome's origin trial covers versions 149-156, with shipping currently targeted for 157. ChatGPT can discover and call WebMCP site tools in the desktop app's built-in browser when the feature is available.

topFixes.name: Scoped permissions
topFixes.recommendation: Declare scoped API permissions where machines can read them: named OAuth scopes in your OpenAPI security schemes, or scopes_supported in RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata. Prose descriptions of roles help humans, but agents need the machine-readable declaration to request least-privilege access.

topFixes.name: REST typed error model
topFixes.recommendation: Document your error responses in your OpenAPI spec: give 4xx and 5xx responses a typed error schema (or use RFC 9457 application/problem+json). A consistent error object with a machine-readable code and a human-readable message lets agents handle failures without guessing.

topFixes.name: ARD discovery
topFixes.recommendation: Publish an Agentic Resource Discovery catalog at /.well-known/ard.json so AI clients can discover your agentic resources (MCP servers, agents, skills, APIs). See https://agenticresourcediscovery.org/

topFixes.name: Brand name discoverability
topFixes.recommendation: Make sure a clean search for your brand name returns your own domain in the top results. If it does not, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen brand-name search by claiming consistent NAP across listings, earning press mentions that link to the canonical domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask the apex domain in search results.

body.name: shopify.com
body.ctaMessage: Strong foundation. Real gaps in the experience layer.
body.agenticSummary: Shopify offers solid developer resource discoverability, but lacks an OpenAPI specification.

checks.name: ARD discovery
checks.details: No /.well-known/ard.json (and no legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json)
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agentic Resource Discovery catalog at /.well-known/ard.json so AI clients can discover your agentic resources (MCP servers, agents, skills, APIs). See https://agenticresourcediscovery.org/

checks.name: AI Catalog discovery
checks.details: No /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - the AI Catalog Standard's discovery path. Bonus only; a catalog at /.well-known/ard.json is scored by the ARD discovery check.
checks.recommendation: Serve a valid catalog at /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - the AI Catalog Standard's own discovery path - so consumers following that spec (see https://ai-catalog.io/) also find you. The same document you serve at /.well-known/ard.json works unchanged.

checks.name: ARD entry validity
checks.details: No catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - entry validity applies only to published catalogs
checks.recommendation: Make every catalog entry fully valid: a domain-anchored urn:air identifier, a displayName, a media type, and exactly one of url or data. Applies to the catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or the legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json.

checks.name: ARD trust manifest
checks.details: No catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - trust metadata applies only to published catalogs
checks.recommendation: Add a trustManifest (verifiable identity, compliance attestations, or signature) to your catalog entries (ard.json, or the legacy ai-catalog.json) so clients can verify your resources with progressive trust.

checks.name: Category share of voice
checks.details: Category share of voice is in beta. It measures whether agents surface you for capability and use-case searches (not just your name). We are tuning it for accuracy before it counts toward your score - coming soon as a Pro check.
checks.recommendation: Build topical authority for your category. Publish comparison pages, 'best X for Y' content, tutorials, and integration guides that rank for generic use-case queries - not just your brand name - so agents surface you when users describe a need.

checks.name: Developer resource discoverability
checks.details: Agent discovered 2 developer-resource types by name (API docs, auth docs) across 3 pages
checks.recommendation: Check whether your developer resources (API docs, OpenAPI spec, auth docs, developer portal, MCP server, SDK documentation) surface in name-based searches. If they do not, use predictable URLs, link them in llms.txt, and include your product name in page titles and headings. This result reflects one search sample.

checks.name: Brand name discoverability
checks.details: shopify.com appears once in brand-name search results for "Shopify e commerce" (position #4 out of 7)
checks.recommendation: Make sure a clean search for your brand name returns your own domain in the top results. If it does not, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen brand-name search by claiming consistent NAP across listings, earning press mentions that link to the canonical domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask the apex domain in search results.

checks.name: Wikipedia / Wikidata entity presence
checks.details: Wikidata Q7501150 (Shopify) verified - draft a Wikipedia page with cited references to complete knowledge graph coverage
checks.recommendation: Establish a Wikipedia article and a Wikidata entity for your brand, with the domain set as the official website (Wikidata property P856) and a corresponding external link on Wikipedia. Wikipedia is the largest single source of citations in ChatGPT and a primary input to Knowledge Graphs across Google, Bing, and LLM training data. Earn third-party press coverage first to satisfy notability, then draft the article with cited references rather than self-promotion.

checks.name: robots.txt AI crawler policy
checks.details: Training: 2/2. Search: 3/3 page/crawler pairs permitted. No applicable crawl or usage restriction found for 5 training and search crawlers (gptbot, claudebot, oai-searchbot, claude-searchbot, perplexitybot) on 1 public page: https://shopify.com/. Declared policy only; absence of a Content Signal expresses no usage preference. Paths outside this sample, live bot access, indexing, and model training are not verified
checks.recommendation: For broad training and search readiness, permit GPTBot and ClaudeBot to collect the affected public pages for training, and OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, and PerplexityBot to crawl them for search. Review the reported URLs, rule lines, and applicable ai-train or search Content Signals. Keep private and account paths restricted. General permissions already count; named directives and Content Signals are optional. The paired search=yes, ai-train=no retains full credit when all evaluated crawling and search are permitted. Other training restrictions mean partial coverage under this benchmark. Usage permission never overrides Disallow. Use the existing agent-user policy and live access results to assess visits.

checks.name: Listed in MCP registries
checks.details: No MCP server detected

checks.name: NPM/PyPI SDK package
checks.details: NPM package found: shopify - "A CLI tool to build for the Shopify platform"
checks.recommendation: Publish a JavaScript/TypeScript SDK package on npm so developers can integrate your API programmatically. In package.json set `repository` to your source repo and `homepage` to your product domain - these links are how agents confirm the package is your official SDK rather than a third-party tool with a similar name.

checks.name: Agent platform configs
checks.details: Could not locate a public repo containing agent configs or rules. If our probes missed it, AI coding agents likely will too - link the repo from your homepage or docs so it's discoverable.
checks.recommendation: Add an AGENTS.md or .cursorrules file to your public GitHub repo with instructions for how AI coding agents should interact with your codebase. Then make sure the repo is documented in the entry-point pages agents read - homepage, docs, and llms.txt - so it can be discovered without guessing.

checks.name: Agent Plugins manifest
checks.details: No Agent Plugins manifest (plugin.json) found in discovered repos
checks.recommendation: Bundle your agent skills and MCP servers as an Agent Plugin: add a plugin.json manifest with the agent-plugins.org $schema and a name. See https://agent-plugins.org/specification

checks.name: Listed on skills.sh
checks.details: 20 official skills published on skills.sh (skills.sh/shopify)
checks.recommendation: Publish agent skills on skills.sh so AI agents can discover your product's capabilities. Create a SKILL.md in your GitHub repo and register it with 'npx skills add'. See skills.sh/docs.

checks.name: Registry branding
checks.details: No MCP server detected
checks.recommendation: Give your MCP server-card (at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json) a display name, an icon or logo, and a description - all three together are what reads as a complete, branded listing agents can present.

checks.name: ChatGPT app listed
checks.details: Found in ChatGPT app directory: "Shopify"
checks.recommendation: Submit your app to the ChatGPT apps / connectors directory (the apps-in-ChatGPT surface) so ChatGPT users can discover and use your product.

checks.name: Sitemap exists
checks.details: Valid sitemap found at /sitemap.xml with 558 entries
checks.recommendation: Add a valid XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml listing all indexable URLs. Include lastmod dates and keep it under 50MB.

checks.name: Content without JavaScript
checks.details: 3431 chars with H1, but 2.5% content ratio is below the 5% target
checks.recommendation: Serve at least 500 characters of meaningful homepage content in raw HTML. Add a clear H1, keep deeper heading levels sequential, and remove excessive non-content markup.

checks.name: Not blocked by bot detection
checks.details: Site accessible to 6 AI agent user-agents
checks.recommendation: Allowlist known AI agent User-Agents (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, DeepSeekBot) in your WAF or bot-detection rules.

checks.name: Agent discovery file
checks.details: Agent discovery file found at /agents.md
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent Skills index at /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json that lists your capabilities, with each skill carrying a name and a description so agents can find and parse what you offer.

checks.name: Agent Skills index conformance (v0.2.0)
checks.details: No /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json - skip v0.2.0 conformance
checks.recommendation: Upgrade /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json to the v0.2.0 schema: add "$schema": "https://schemas.agentskills.io/discovery/0.2.0/schema.json", and give every entry a type (skill-md or archive), url, and digest. Use "digest": "sha256:<64 lowercase hex chars>" (e.g. "digest": "sha256:a3f1...") - a bare "sha256": "<hex>" field is also accepted. Compute the value from the artifact's raw bytes.

checks.name: A2A / agent-card
checks.details: No A2A agent card found at /.well-known/agent-card.json
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json describing your agent's capabilities, skills, and contact endpoint.

checks.name: pricing.md exists
checks.details: No pricing.md found - agents need machine-readable pricing to compare products and make purchase recommendations
checks.recommendation: Create a /pricing.md file with your pricing tiers, features, and limits in plain markdown. This lets AI agents compare costs and recommend plans without scraping HTML pricing pages.

checks.name: NLWeb Schema Feeds
checks.details: No schemamap: directive in robots.txt
checks.recommendation: Add a schemamap: directive to robots.txt pointing to a Schema Map XML file listing your structured data feeds (JSONL/RSS). See the NLWeb Schema Feeds spec.

checks.name: MCP well-known discovery
checks.details: MCP server at https://help.shopify.com/mcp - consider adding /.well-known/mcp for standard discovery
checks.recommendation: Serve your MCP server at /.well-known/mcp, publish a server-card.json at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, or reference it in llms.txt so agents can discover it automatically without manual URL input.

checks.name: Agent mode view
checks.details: ?mode=agent returns same content as homepage (no dedicated agent view)
checks.recommendation: Add a ?mode=agent query parameter to your homepage that returns a structured, machine-readable view with API endpoints, authentication info, and key capabilities instead of marketing HTML.

checks.name: HTTP Link headers (RFC 8288)
checks.details: No HTTP Link response headers (RFC 8288) found
checks.recommendation: Add HTTP Link: response headers (RFC 8288) advertising your sitemap, markdown alternates, API service descriptions, and API catalog. Example: Link: </sitemap.xml>; rel="sitemap", </index.md>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown".

checks.name: Markdown URL fallback
checks.details: Homepage does not support the .md suffix. Probed https://shopify.com/index.md and it did not return markdown (expected text/markdown content-type or a heading-led non-HTML body). Serve /index.md so agents can fetch one canonical markdown URL for the site root.
checks.recommendation: Let agents fetch markdown by appending .md to page URLs. Required for any credit: serve a markdown homepage at /index.md. For full credit (2/2): also serve a .md twin for each content page (e.g. /docs/auth -> /docs/auth.md). Content-Type should be text/markdown and the body should start with a top-level heading (not HTML).

checks.name: Modular llms.txt per product area
checks.details: No section-level llms.txt files found (optional)
checks.recommendation: Add per-section llms.txt files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt, /developers/llms.txt) so agents can fetch scoped context for specific product areas instead of the whole manual.

checks.name: Sitemap freshness (lastmod)
checks.details: 100% of 500 sampled sitemap entries carry lastmod; newest is 2 day(s) old
checks.recommendation: Add <lastmod> dates (W3C datetime, e.g. 2026-08-01) to your sitemap entries and update them when content actually changes. Aim for lastmod on at least half your entries with the newest within the last year. Verify with `curl https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml | grep lastmod`.

checks.name: robots.txt agent-user policy
checks.details: No applicable crawl or usage restriction found for 3 user-triggered agents (chatgpt-user, claude-user, perplexity-user) on 1 public page: https://shopify.com/. Declared policy only; absence of a Content Signal expresses no usage preference. Paths outside this sample, live bot access, indexing, and model training are not verified
checks.recommendation: Review the matched homepage rules for ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, and Perplexity-User. If you intend to permit these requests, remove or narrow the reported restriction while keeping private paths protected. Review applicable ai-input=no declarations if answer-time use is intended. This check reports declared permission; a robots.txt change alone does not establish live access.

checks.name: llms.txt exists
checks.details: Found the llms.txt at https://shopify.dev/llms.txt.
checks.recommendation: Create an llms.txt file at your domain root (/llms.txt) - the AI equivalent of robots.txt. Write at least 100 characters of real content: what your product is, what it does, and links to your key docs. Then verify it with `curl https://yourdomain.com/llms.txt` - you should see your text, not HTML. If your app returns its homepage for every URL (common with single-page apps), add a static file route so the raw text is served. A placeholder with just a heading earns no credit.

checks.name: llms.txt formatting
checks.details: The llms.txt is well-formatted: 86 lines with markdown links, 12,516 characters in total.
checks.recommendation: Format your llms.txt as a navigation index: start with a markdown heading, include markdown links to deeper resources, and keep it under 30,000 characters. If you have more to say, move long-form content into /llms-full.txt or per-section files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt) and link to them from the main index.

checks.name: JSON-LD structured data
checks.details: JSON-LD found (1 block(s)) but no identity type - use SoftwareApplication, Product, Organization, Person, or Article so agents can tell what this site is
checks.recommendation: Add JSON-LD structured data to your homepage using the identity type that matches your site - SoftwareApplication for products, Organization or LocalBusiness for companies, Person for personal sites, Article for blogs - with name, description, url, and type-appropriate fields (offers, sameAs, author) so AI can parse your identity programmatically.

Fix or remove any dead link; agents that follow the index treat a broken link as a dead end.

checks.name: Markdown alternate link

checks.name: Markdown frontmatter metadata
checks.details: None of the 1 served markdown doc opens with a --- frontmatter block. Add title, description, canonical, and last-updated so agents get metadata without scraping.
checks.recommendation: Open your served markdown docs with a --- frontmatter block carrying title plus at least one of description, canonical, or last-updated. Agents read frontmatter as document metadata without scraping. A Link: rel="canonical" response header also satisfies the canonical slot.

checks.name: Redirect hygiene
checks.details: No meta-refresh stubs, JavaScript-redirect stubs, or cross-domain hops across 1 checked page
checks.recommendation: Replace meta-refresh and JavaScript-only redirects with real HTTP 301/302 redirects. Non-JS agents never execute `location.href` or wait for a meta refresh - they see only the stub page. Verify with `curl -sI <url>` - you should see a Location header, not a 200 with a near-empty body.

checks.name: Page token budget

checks.recommendation: Keep each page's extracted text under ~100K characters (~25K tokens) so it fits an agent's context window without truncation. Split oversized reference pages into focused per-topic documents and link them from an index. Check a page with `curl -s <url> | wc -c` and remember agents read the extracted text, not the raw HTML.

checks.name: Code fence validity
checks.details: Code fences balanced across 1 markdown document
checks.recommendation: Close every fenced code block (``` or ~~~) in your served markdown. CommonMark treats everything after an unclosed fence as code, so an agent parsing the document silently loses the rest of it. Count fence lines per file - the total must be even.

checks.name: Markdown content negotiation (acceptmarkdown.com)

checks.details: Category share of voice is in beta. It measures whether agents surface you for capability and use-case searches (not just your name). We are tuning it for accuracy before it counts toward your score - coming soon as a Pro check.
checks.recommendation: Build topical authority for your category. Publish comparison pages, 'best X for Y' content, tutorials, and integration guides that rank for generic use-case queries - not just your brand name - so agents surface you when users describe a need.

checks.name: Developer resource discoverability
checks.details: Agent discovered 1 developer-resource type by name (auth docs) across 5 pages
checks.recommendation: Check whether your developer resources (API docs, OpenAPI spec, auth docs, developer portal, MCP server, SDK documentation) surface in name-based searches. If they do not, use predictable URLs, link them in llms.txt, and include your product name in page titles and headings. This result reflects one search sample.

checks.name: Brand name discoverability
checks.details: github.com appears at position #1 in a clean brand-name search for "GitHub developer tools" (6 total matches)
checks.recommendation: Make sure a clean search for your brand name returns your own domain in the top results. If it does not, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen brand-name search by claiming consistent NAP across listings, earning press mentions that link to the canonical domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask the apex domain in search results.

checks.name: Wikipedia / Wikidata entity presence
checks.details: Wikipedia "GitHub" and Wikidata Q364 both verified - domain confirmed on both sources
checks.recommendation: Establish a Wikipedia article and a Wikidata entity for your brand, with the domain set as the official website (Wikidata property P856) and a corresponding external link on Wikipedia. Wikipedia is the largest single source of citations in ChatGPT and a primary input to Knowledge Graphs across Google, Bing, and LLM training data. Earn third-party press coverage first to satisfy notability, then draft the article with cited references rather than self-promotion.

checks.name: robots.txt AI crawler policy
checks.details: Training: 2/2. Search: 3/3 page/crawler pairs permitted. No applicable crawl or usage restriction found for 5 training and search crawlers (gptbot, claudebot, oai-searchbot, claude-searchbot, perplexitybot) on 1 public page: https://github.com/. Declared policy only; absence of a Content Signal expresses no usage preference. Paths outside this sample, live bot access, indexing, and model training are not verified. Policy excerpts (only evaluated uses and agents affect this score): gptbot,oai-searchbot,claudebot,anthropic-ai,perplexitybot: Allow: /$, Allow: /about, Allow: /customer-stories, Allow: /enterprise, Allow: /features, Allow: /marketplace; bytespider: Disallow: /
checks.recommendation: For broad training and search readiness, permit GPTBot and ClaudeBot to collect the affected public pages for training, and OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, and PerplexityBot to crawl them for search. Review the reported URLs, rule lines, and applicable ai-train or search Content Signals. Keep private and account paths restricted. General permissions already count; named directives and Content Signals are optional. The paired search=yes, ai-train=no retains full credit when all evaluated crawling and search are permitted. Other training restrictions mean partial coverage under this benchmark. Usage permission never overrides Disallow. Use the existing agent-user policy and live access results to assess visits.

Verify both with `curl -sS -L -i -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://yourdomain.com/` and `curl -sS -L -i -H 'Accept: text/html' https://yourdomain.com/`. checks.name: Category share of voice
checks.details: Category share of voice is in beta. It measures whether agents surface you for capability and use-case searches (not just your name). We are tuning it for accuracy before it counts toward your score - coming soon as a Pro check.
checks.recommendation: Build topical authority for your category. Publish comparison pages, 'best X for Y' content, tutorials, and integration guides that rank for generic use-case queries - not just your brand name - so agents surface you when users describe a need.

checks.name: Developer resource discoverability
checks.details: Agent discovered 2 developer-resource types by name (MCP server, OpenAPI spec) across 5 pages
checks.recommendation: Check whether your developer resources (API docs, OpenAPI spec, auth docs, developer portal, MCP server, SDK documentation) surface in name-based searches. If they do not, use predictable URLs, link them in llms.txt, and include your product name in page titles and headings. This result reflects one search sample.

checks.name: Brand name discoverability
checks.details: twilio.com appears at position #1 in a clean brand-name search for "Twilio communication support" (8 total matches)
checks.recommendation: Make sure a clean search for your brand name returns your own domain in the top results. If it does not, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen brand-name search by claiming consistent NAP across listings, earning press mentions that link to the canonical domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask the apex domain in search results.

checks.name: Wikipedia / Wikidata entity presence
checks.details: Wikipedia "Twilio" and Wikidata Q7858039 both verified - domain confirmed on both sources
checks.recommendation: Establish a Wikipedia article and a Wikidata entity for your brand, with the domain set as the official website (Wikidata property P856) and a corresponding external link on Wikipedia. Wikipedia is the largest single source of citations in ChatGPT and a primary input to Knowledge Graphs across Google, Bing, and LLM training data. Earn third-party press coverage first to satisfy notability, then draft the article with cited references rather than self-promotion.

checks.name: robots.txt AI crawler policy
checks.details: Training: 0/2. Search: 3/3 page/crawler pairs permitted. Applicable Content Signals declare search=yes, ai-train=no. Training is refused, but this policy retains full credit because every evaluated page permits crawling and search. Checked 5 training and search crawlers (gptbot, claudebot, oai-searchbot, claude-searchbot, perplexitybot) on 1 public page. Declared policy only; live access, indexing, and model training are not verified. Policy excerpts (only evaluated uses and agents affect this score): *: ai-train=no, search=yes, ai-input=yes
checks.recommendation: For broad training and search readiness, permit GPTBot and ClaudeBot to collect the affected public pages for training, and OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, and PerplexityBot to crawl them for search. Review the reported URLs, rule lines, and applicable ai-train or search Content Signals. Keep private and account paths restricted. General permissions already count; named directives and Content Signals are optional. The paired search=yes, ai-train=no retains full credit when all evaluated crawling and search are permitted. Other training restrictions mean partial coverage under this benchmark. Usage permission never overrides Disallow. Use the existing agent-user policy and live access results to assess visits.

topFixes.name: Scoped permissions

topFixes.name: WebMCP support
topFixes.recommendation: Expose in-page tools through WebMCP, a proposed web standard for browser agents. Register tools with document.modelContext.registerTool() and use navigator.modelContext only as a trailing compatibility fallback. Declarative forms with toolname and tooldescription provide server-rendered evidence, but remain a preview and should not be your only tool surface. Chrome's origin trial covers versions 149-156, with shipping currently targeted for 157. topFixes.name: Schema type breadth

checks.name: ARD discovery
checks.details: No /.well-known/ard.json (and no legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json)
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agentic Resource Discovery catalog at /.well-known/ard.json so AI clients can discover your agentic resources (MCP servers, agents, skills, APIs). See https://agenticresourcediscovery.org/

checks.name: AI Catalog discovery
checks.details: No /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - the AI Catalog Standard's discovery path. Bonus only; a catalog at /.well-known/ard.json is scored by the ARD discovery check.
checks.recommendation: Serve a valid catalog at /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - the AI Catalog Standard's own discovery path - so consumers following that spec (see https://ai-catalog.io/) also find you. The same document you serve at /.well-known/ard.json works unchanged.

checks.name: ARD entry validity
checks.details: No catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - entry validity applies only to published catalogs
checks.recommendation: Make every catalog entry fully valid: a domain-anchored urn:air identifier, a displayName, a media type, and exactly one of url or data. Applies to the catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or the legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json.

checks.name: ARD trust manifest
checks.details: No catalog at /.well-known/ard.json or /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - trust metadata applies only to published catalogs
checks.recommendation: Add a trustManifest (verifiable identity, compliance attestations, or signature) to your catalog entries (ard.json, or the legacy ai-catalog.json) so clients can verify your resources with progressive trust.

checks.name: Category share of voice
checks.details: Category share of voice is in beta. It measures whether agents surface you for capability and use-case searches (not just your name). We are tuning it for accuracy before it counts toward your score - coming soon as a Pro check.
checks.recommendation: Build topical authority for your category. Publish comparison pages, 'best X for Y' content, tutorials, and integration guides that rank for generic use-case queries - not just your brand name - so agents surface you when users describe a need.

checks.name: Developer resource discoverability
checks.details: Agent found 4 pages by name but no recognizable developer-resource type. Found on site but absent from this search sample: MCP server. Not found in this search sample: OpenAPI spec, auth docs, SDK documentation
checks.recommendation: Check whether your developer resources (API docs, OpenAPI spec, auth docs, developer portal, MCP server, SDK documentation) surface in name-based searches. If they do not, use predictable URLs, link them in llms.txt, and include your product name in page titles and headings. This result reflects one search sample.

checks.name: Brand name discoverability
checks.details: notion.com appears once in brand-name search results for "Notion" (position #4 out of 6)
checks.recommendation: Make sure a clean search for your brand name returns your own domain in the top results. If it does not, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen brand-name search by claiming consistent NAP across listings, earning press mentions that link to the canonical domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask the apex domain in search results.

checks.name: Wikipedia / Wikidata entity presence
checks.details: Wikipedia "Notion (productivity software)" and Wikidata Q60747998 both verified - domain confirmed on both sources
checks.recommendation: Establish a Wikipedia article and a Wikidata entity for your brand, with the domain set as the official website (Wikidata property P856) and a corresponding external link on Wikipedia. Wikipedia is the largest single source of citations in ChatGPT and a primary input to Knowledge Graphs across Google, Bing, and LLM training data. Earn third-party press coverage first to satisfy notability, then draft the article with cited references rather than self-promotion.

checks.name: robots.txt AI crawler policy
checks.details: Training: 2/2. Search: 3/3 page/crawler pairs permitted. No applicable crawl or usage restriction found for 5 training and search crawlers (gptbot, claudebot, oai-searchbot, claude-searchbot, perplexitybot) on 1 public page: https://notion.com/. Declared policy only; absence of a Content Signal expresses no usage preference. Paths outside this sample, live bot access, indexing, and model training are not verified
checks.recommendation: For broad training and search readiness, permit GPTBot and ClaudeBot to collect the affected public pages for training, and OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, and PerplexityBot to crawl them for search. Review the reported URLs, rule lines, and applicable ai-train or search Content Signals. Keep private and account paths restricted. General permissions already count; named directives and Content Signals are optional. The paired search=yes, ai-train=no retains full credit when all evaluated crawling and search are permitted. Other training restrictions mean partial coverage under this benchmark. Usage permission never overrides Disallow. Use the existing agent-user policy and live access results to assess visits.

checks.name: Listed in MCP registries
checks.details: Verified in 2 registries: Smithery (notion) [entry-to-product], npm (@notionhq/notion-mcp-server) [npm-scope] - 3841 agent uses, verified
checks.recommendation: Register your MCP server on Smithery (smithery.ai) or mcp.so so agent platforms can discover your tools. Link the registry entry from your homepage or docs for bi-directional verification.

checks.name: NPM/PyPI SDK package
checks.details: NPM package found: notion-types - "TypeScript types for core Notion data structures."
checks.recommendation: Publish a JavaScript/TypeScript SDK package on npm so developers can integrate your API programmatically. In package.json set `repository` to your source repo and `homepage` to your product domain - these links are how agents confirm the package is your official SDK rather than a third-party tool with a similar name.

checks.name: Agent platform configs
checks.details: Agent config found: github.com/makenotion/notion-sdk-js/blob/main/AGENTS.md
checks.recommendation: Add an AGENTS.md or .cursorrules file to your public GitHub repo with instructions for how AI coding agents should interact with your codebase. Then make sure the repo is documented in the entry-point pages agents read - homepage, docs, and llms.txt - so it can be discovered without guessing.

checks.name: Agent Plugins manifest
checks.details: No Agent Plugins manifest (plugin.json) found in discovered repos
checks.recommendation: Bundle your agent skills and MCP servers as an Agent Plugin: add a plugin.json manifest with the agent-plugins.org $schema and a name. See https://agent-plugins.org/specification

checks.name: Listed on skills.sh
checks.details: No official skills self-published on skills.sh (100 community skills with potential relation to this domain found, but only self-published official skills count)
checks.recommendation: Publish agent skills on skills.sh so AI agents can discover your product's capabilities. Create a SKILL.md in your GitHub repo and register it with 'npx skills add'. See skills.sh/docs.

checks.name: Registry branding
checks.details: MCP manifest has full branding (name, icon, description) at /.well-known/mcp.json
checks.recommendation: Give your MCP server-card (at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json) a display name, an icon or logo, and a description - all three together are what reads as a complete, branded listing agents can present.

checks.name: ChatGPT app listed
checks.details: Found in ChatGPT app directory: "Notion"
checks.recommendation: Submit your app to the ChatGPT apps / connectors directory (the apps-in-ChatGPT surface) so ChatGPT users can discover and use your product.

checks.name: Sitemap exists
checks.details: Valid sitemap found at https://www.notion.com/sitemap.xml with multiple sitemaps entries
checks.recommendation: Add a valid XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml listing all indexable URLs. Include lastmod dates and keep it under 50MB.

checks.name: Content without JavaScript
checks.details: 778 chars with H1, but 0.6% content ratio is below the 5% target
checks.recommendation: Serve at least 500 characters of meaningful homepage content in raw HTML. Add a clear H1, keep deeper heading levels sequential, and remove excessive non-content markup.

checks.name: Not blocked by bot detection
checks.details: Site accessible to 6 AI agent user-agents
checks.recommendation: Allowlist known AI agent User-Agents (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, DeepSeekBot) in your WAF or bot-detection rules.

checks.name: Agent discovery file
checks.details: No agent discovery file found
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent Skills index at /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json that lists your capabilities, with each skill carrying a name and a description so agents can find and parse what you offer.

checks.name: Agent Skills index conformance (v0.2.0)
checks.details: No /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json - skip v0.2.0 conformance
checks.recommendation: Upgrade /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json to the v0.2.0 schema: add "$schema": "https://schemas.agentskills.io/discovery/0.2.0/schema.json", and give every entry a type (skill-md or archive), url, and digest. Use "digest": "sha256:<64 lowercase hex chars>" (e.g. "digest": "sha256:a3f1...") - a bare "sha256": "<hex>" field is also accepted. Compute the value from the artifact's raw bytes.

checks.name: A2A / agent-card
checks.details: No A2A agent card found at /.well-known/agent-card.json
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json describing your agent's capabilities, skills, and contact endpoint.

checks.name: pricing.md exists
checks.details: No pricing.md found - agents need machine-readable pricing to compare products and make purchase recommendations
checks.recommendation: Create a /pricing.md file with your pricing tiers, features, and limits in plain markdown. This lets AI agents compare costs and recommend plans without scraping HTML pricing pages.

checks.name: NLWeb Schema Feeds
checks.details: No schemamap: directive in robots.txt
checks.recommendation: Add a schemamap: directive to robots.txt pointing to a Schema Map XML file listing your structured data feeds (JSONL/RSS). See the NLWeb Schema Feeds spec.

checks.name: MCP well-known discovery
checks.details: MCP server at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp - consider adding /.well-known/mcp for standard discovery
checks.recommendation: Serve your MCP server at /.well-known/mcp, publish a server-card.json at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, or reference it in llms.txt so agents can discover it automatically without manual URL input.

checks.name: Agent mode view
checks.details: ?mode=agent returns same content as homepage (no dedicated agent view)
checks.recommendation: Add a ?mode=agent query parameter to your homepage that returns a structured, machine-readable view with API endpoints, authentication info, and key capabilities instead of marketing HTML.

checks.name: HTTP Link headers (RFC 8288)
checks.details: No HTTP Link response headers (RFC 8288) found
checks.recommendation: Add HTTP Link: response headers (RFC 8288) advertising your sitemap, markdown alternates, API service descriptions, and API catalog. Example: Link: </sitemap.xml>; rel="sitemap", </index.md>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown".

checks.name: Markdown URL fallback
checks.details: Homepage does not support the .md suffix. Probed https://notion.com/index.md and it did not return markdown (expected text/markdown content-type or a heading-led non-HTML body). Serve /index.md so agents can fetch one canonical markdown URL for the site root.
checks.recommendation: Let agents fetch markdown by appending .md to page URLs. Required for any credit: serve a markdown homepage at /index.md. For full credit (2/2): also serve a .md twin for each content page (e.g. /docs/auth -> /docs/auth.md). Content-Type should be text/markdown and the body should start with a top-level heading (not HTML).

checks.name: Modular llms.txt per product area
checks.details: No section-level llms.txt files found (optional)
checks.recommendation: Add per-section llms.txt files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt, /developers/llms.txt) so agents can fetch scoped context for specific product areas instead of the whole manual.

checks.name: Sitemap freshness (lastmod)
checks.details: None of the 116 sampled sitemap entries carries a lastmod date. Add <lastmod> (W3C datetime) so agents can prioritize fresh content.
checks.recommendation: Add <lastmod> dates (W3C datetime, e.g. 2026-08-01) to your sitemap entries and update them when content actually changes. Aim for lastmod on at least half your entries with the newest within the last year. Verify with `curl https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml | grep lastmod`.

checks.name: robots.txt agent-user policy
checks.details: No applicable crawl or usage restriction found for 3 user-triggered agents (chatgpt-user, claude-user, perplexity-user) on 1 public page: https://notion.com/. Declared policy only; absence of a Content Signal expresses no usage preference. Paths outside this sample, live bot access, indexing, and model training are not verified
checks.recommendation: Review the matched homepage rules for ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, and Perplexity-User. If you intend to permit these requests, remove or narrow the reported restriction while keeping private paths protected. Review applicable ai-input=no declarations if answer-time use is intended. This check reports declared permission; a robots.txt change alone does not establish live access.

checks.name: llms.txt exists
checks.details: Found the llms.txt at https://developers.notion.com/llms.txt.
checks.recommendation: Create an llms.txt file at your domain root (/llms.txt) - the AI equivalent of robots.txt. Write at least 100 characters of real content: what your product is, what it does, and links to your key docs. Then verify it with `curl https://yourdomain.com/llms.txt` - you should see your text, not HTML. If your app returns its homepage for every URL (common with single-page apps), add a static file route so the raw text is served. A placeholder with just a heading earns no credit.

checks.name: llms.txt formatting
checks.details: The llms.txt is well-formatted: 58 lines with markdown links, 6,799 characters in total.
checks.recommendation: Format your llms.txt as a navigation index: start with a markdown heading, include markdown links to deeper resources, and keep it under 30,000 characters. If you have more to say, move long-form content into /llms-full.txt or per-section files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt) and link to them from the main index.

checks.name: JSON-LD structured data
checks.details: No JSON-LD structured data found on homepage
checks.recommendation: Add JSON-LD structured data to your homepage using the identity type that matches your site - SoftwareApplication for products, Organization or LocalBusiness for companies, Person for personal sites, Article for blogs - with name, description, url, and type-appropriate fields (offers, sameAs, author) so AI can parse your identity programmatically.

If your app returns the homepage shell for unknown paths (common with single-page apps), a 200 status is not proof: check the body. Fix or remove any dead link; agents that follow the index treat a broken link as a dead end.

checks.name: Markdown alternate link
checks.details: No sampled page advertises a markdown alternate. Add <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="..."> (or the equivalent Link response header) pointing at a markdown twin of the page.

Verify the target with `curl -s <href>` and check the body starts with a heading, not <!doctype html>.

checks.name: Markdown frontmatter metadata

checks.recommendation: Open your served markdown docs with a --- frontmatter block carrying title plus at least one of description, canonical, or last-updated. Agents read frontmatter as document metadata without scraping. A Link: rel="canonical" response header also satisfies the canonical slot.

checks.name: Redirect hygiene
checks.details: No meta-refresh stubs, JavaScript-redirect stubs, or cross-domain hops across 1 checked page
checks.recommendation: Replace meta-refresh and JavaScript-only redirects with real HTTP 301/302 redirects. Non-JS agents never execute `location.href` or wait for a meta refresh - they see only the stub page. Verify with `curl -sI <url>` - you should see a Location header, not a 200 with a near-empty body.

checks.name: Page token budget
checks.details: All 1 measured page fit an agent context budget (largest ~1K tokens)
checks.recommendation: Keep each page's extracted text under ~100K characters (~25K tokens) so it fits an agent's context window without truncation. Split oversized reference pages into focused per-topic documents and link them from an index. Check a page with `curl -s <url> | wc -c` and remember agents read the extracted text, not the raw HTML.

checks.name: Code fence validity
checks.details: Code fences balanced across 1 markdown document
checks.recommendation: Close every fenced code block (``` or ~~~) in your served markdown. CommonMark treats everything after an unclosed fence as code, so an agent parsing the document silently loses the rest of it. Count fence lines per file - the total must be even.
